rules.text: Lattice Studio (`python -m lattice.studio PROJECT_DIR`) serves one project directory (`REQUIREMENTS.md`, `spec.py`, `spec.trace.json`) over a JSON API on 127.0.0.1, with no login. These rules are what `lattice/studio/server.py` and `tests/studio/test_server.py` establish; `lattice/studio/API.md` is the contract.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements

rules.text: GET /api/model answers 200 with the project (`name`: `[project] name` of its studio.toml, else the directory's name; `git_head`: the short id of the repository's HEAD), the rules of the trace with their status and links, the full REQUIREMENTS.md text, the data model's tables, `app` (`configured`, `check_running`, `last_check`) and the change records (`id`, `request`, `status`).
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > The model

rules.text: A change that is drafting, ready, rejected, cancelled or failed never writes the project's files: GET /api/model keeps answering the same markdown and `git_head` until a change is accepted.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > The model

rules.text: POST /api/changes {"request": ...} answers 200 with the change's id (`c1`, then `c2`, ... in order) and drafts it in the background: its status starts as `drafting`, goes through `checking`, and ends `ready` (or `failed`). GET /api/changes/{id} answers the change record.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: GET /api/changes/{id}?wait=S (S from 0 to 60 seconds) answers once the change's background job has finished, or after S seconds; a `wait` that is not such a number answers 422.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: A ready change's record names the rules its edit added, changed and removed, and `checks.valid` says whether its drafted spec validates.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: POST /api/changes/{id}/accept on a ready, valid change writes REQUIREMENTS.md, spec.py and spec.trace.json and makes exactly one git commit of those files on top of HEAD, with the message `spec: <request>` and the trailer; it answers 200 with the commit id and the message. Other files of the project are not committed.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: After an accept, GET /api/model answers the new markdown, `git_head` the new commit, and the change's status `accepted`.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: A change can be accepted once: a second accept answers 409 ("change <id> is accepted, not ready").
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: A proposal drafted on files that have changed since (for example because another change was accepted) is stale: its accept answers 409 ("the spec changed since this proposal") and writes nothing.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: POST /api/changes/{id}/reject answers 200 {"ok": true} and the change's status becomes `rejected`; an accept after it answers 409. Rejecting an accepted change answers 409 ("change <id> is already accepted").
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: A change rejected while it is still drafting or checking stays rejected: its background job's result is dropped and it can never be accepted.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: DELETE /api/changes/{id} cancels a change that is still drafting or checking: it answers 200 {"ok": true, "status": "cancelled"}, the change stays `cancelled` after its background job ends, and it can never be accepted. Cancelling any other change (ready, failed, cancelled, accepted, rejected) answers 409.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: A change whose markdown edit or draft fails ends `failed` with the error in `error`; it cannot be accepted (409) or cancelled (409).
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Change sets

rules.text: POST /api/changes with "parent": "<id>" drafts a follow-up on top of the parent's proposal (its markdown already holds the parent's edit). The parent must be ready, else 409.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Follow-ups

rules.text: When the follow-up becomes ready, it supersedes its parent: the parent's status becomes `rejected` and its `superseded_by` names the follow-up; a further follow-up on that parent then answers 409.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Follow-ups

rules.text: Accepting the follow-up writes the parent's edit and its own in one commit.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Follow-ups

rules.text: A request body that is not a JSON object answers 400; an empty `request` (or `question` for POST /api/ask) answers 422 with a `detail`.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Errors

rules.text: An unknown change id answers 404 ("no change <id>") on GET, DELETE, accept and reject, and as a follow-up's parent; an unknown /api/ path answers 404 ("no such route").
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Errors

rules.text: Every error answer is a JSON object `{"detail": "..."}`.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Errors

rules.text: POST /api/ask {"question": ...} answers 200 with `kind` (yes, no, value or not_specified), `answer`, `explanation` and `citations` checked against the spec; without an app configured, `verified` is null.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Ask

rules.text: An answer's content comes from the LLM.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Ask

rules.text: Any other GET path serves a file of the web UI directory (`/` is index.html); a path that resolves outside that directory, or names no file, answers 404 {"detail": "not found"}.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > The web UI

rules.text: POST /api/check runs the full check of the current spec against the configured app in the background and reports it in `app.last_check`.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Not covered here

rules.text: The chat runs on Claude Code sessions (POST /api/session and the routes under it).
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Not covered here

rules.text: A change's impact is checked against the configured app when `studio.toml` hooks one up.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Not covered here

rules.text: Outside a git repository, accept writes the files and answers `commit: null` with a note; a git failure answers 500 after the files are written.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Not covered here

rules.text: GET /api/projects answers 200 with every project the server serves, in order: `name`, `root`, `git_head`, `spec` (whether `spec.py` and `spec.trace.json` are present), `app_configured`, `last_check` (null until a check has run) and `default`. A server over one directory lists that one project, as the default.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Projects

rules.text: Every /api/ route is also served under /p/<name>/api/... for a served project: /p/<name>/api/model answers what the bare /api/model answers for the default project, and a change made through one path is the same change through the other.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Projects

rules.text: A /p/<name>/ path whose name is no served project answers 404 ("no such project").
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Projects

rules.text: Projects served by one server do not share change sets: each project numbers its own changes from `c1`, and a change made in one project is not visible in another.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Projects

rules.text: POST /api/rebuild {"changes": [...]} on accepted changes answers 200 with the rebuild's id (`b1`, then `b2`, ... in order) and runs it in the background in a new git worktree, on a new branch `rebuild/<first change id>` (`-2`, `-3`, ... when that branch exists) made from HEAD. GET /api/rebuild/{id} answers its record; with ?wait=S (S from 0 to 60 seconds) it answers once the rebuild has finished, or after S seconds.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Rebuild

rules.text: Each round, the coding agent edits the code in the worktree, then Studio itself runs the project's gate commands there: a round passes only when every gate exits 0. A failing round's findings, taken from the gates' output, are in the round's record with each gate's exit code, and they are the next round's brief.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Rebuild

rules.text: A round in which the agent edited REQUIREMENTS.md, spec.py or spec.trace.json fails with the finding "spec files were edited", and those files are restored to the base commit's content.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Rebuild

rules.text: When a round passes, the rebuild ends `passed` with exactly one commit on its branch, on top of the base commit, with the message `build: <requests>` and a `Lattice-Rebuild:` trailer, holding the files the rounds changed. After `max_rounds` failing rounds it ends `gave_up`, with nothing committed.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Rebuild

rules.text: A rebuild never merges and never moves the owner's checkout: after it passes, GET /api/model answers the same markdown and `git_head` as before, and the record's `merge_hint` says how to merge the branch.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Rebuild

rules.text: An accepted change carries `build` in GET /api/model: `not_built` before any rebuild and after a stopped one, `rebuilding` while one runs, `built` with its `rebuild_id`, `branch` and `commit` once one passed, and `gave_up` when one gave up. A gave-up change can be rebuilt again.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Rebuild

rules.text: POST /api/rebuild for a change that is not accepted answers 409 ("change <id> is <status>, not accepted"), for a change already rebuilding or built 409 ("change <id> is already <state>"), and while a rebuild runs another one in the same project answers 409 ("a rebuild is already running in this project (<id>)"). An unknown change answers 404 ("no change <id>") and a body without a non-empty list of change ids, or with `max_rounds` below 1, answers 422.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Rebuild

rules.text: DELETE /api/rebuild/{id} stops a queued or running rebuild: it answers {"id": ..., "status": "stopped"}, its worktree is removed, its branch too when it has no commit of its own, and its changes go back to `not_built`. DELETE on a finished rebuild answers 409 ("cannot stop a rebuild that is <status>"); an unknown rebuild id answers 404 ("no rebuild <id>") on GET and DELETE.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Rebuild

rules.text: GET /api/projects reports `capabilities.rebuild`: true when the project's `[rebuild]` table names a git repository and gate commands that resolve, and its agent (Claude Code, or the test-only stub) can run.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Rebuild

rules.text: GET /api/areas answers the spec's areas: its rules grouped by their top-level requirements section, in document order, each with `id`, `title`, `rules`, `scenarios` (the scenarios linked to those rules), `failing` (null until a check of the target branch ran) and `status` (`not_built`, `partial`, `built` or `building`), then the area `all`; ?branch=B answers them for target branch B.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Build from spec

rules.text: POST /api/rebuild {"scope": {"area": id} | {"rules": [ids]} | "all"} needs no accepted change: Studio first runs the gates once (the baseline), and the scope's targets are the baseline's failing checks linked to the scope's rules; the record carries `scope`, `baseline` (its findings, each with its rules and whether it is in scope) and the targets.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Build from spec

rules.text: A scoped round passes when every target of the scope passes and no check that passed in the baseline fails (a regression), decided by Studio from the gate findings; checks outside the scope that failed in the baseline may stay failing. Each round records `scope_passing`, `scope_total`, `regressions` and `newly_fixed`.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Build from spec

rules.text: Scoped builds land on a target branch, by default `build/<project>`, created from HEAD on first use: each build starts from the target's tip and, when it passes, the target is fast-forwarded to its commit, so areas accumulate; the owner's branch and checkout never move, and GET /api/areas reports the target's areas from the build's results.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Build from spec

rules.text: A scope with nothing failing after the baseline answers 409 ("nothing to build: the checks in this scope already pass") and leaves no rebuild record; an unknown area or rule answers 404 ("no area <id>", "no rule <id>"), a malformed scope 422, and a `branch` without a scope 422 ("branch needs a scope").
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Build from spec

rules.text: GET /api/branches answers the repository's local branches (`name`, `head`, `current`, `protected`, `ahead_of_base`, `is_integration`) with `current_branch`, `protected` and `default_target`.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Build from spec

rules.text: POST /api/rebuild with "branch": {"name", "create", "from"} targets that branch: an unknown branch answers 404 (code `no_branch`), an existing one with create 409 (`branch_exists`, nothing overwritten), an unknown `from` 404 (`no_ref`), an invalid name 422 (`branch_name_invalid`); a protected branch (409 `branch_protected`) or the branch checked out in the owner's worktree (409 `branch_checked_out`) is refused unless the request confirms it, and even then a worktree with changes answers 409 (`tree_dirty`).
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Build from spec

rules.text: GET /api/projects reports `capabilities.build_from_spec`, true when the project can rebuild.
rules.section: Lattice Studio server: requirements > Build from spec

unchecked.R24: POST /api/check needs a configured app; tests/studio/test_server.py covers it
unchecked.R25: the chat sessions need the claude binary; tests/studio/test_session.py covers them
unchecked.R26: the change impact needs a configured app; tests/studio/test_server.py covers it
unchecked.R27: accept outside git or on a git failure needs a different repository; tests/studio/test_server.py covers the first
unchecked.R31: the harness serves one project directory; tests/studio/test_projects.py covers isolation between two projects
